increment_paragraph: **OPENSSL-PEM-CALLBACK-ARM (2026-11-18).** A literal-argument premise may stand beside synchronous invocations that are a declaration's only retaining clauses (contract spec C04.5 "Beside a synchronous invocation", C04.19 placement, grammar G05, new gateway rule 57); every other retaining clause beside a premise still rejects. Route G's premise rewrite (legacy_literal_premise) now treats a withheld retaining declaration as a contracted callee, so an unmet premise renames the call before the callback route reads it; with that change reverted the fixture's non-null-x call was measured Safe. pem.qv: both PEM readers drop the cb = 0 premise and state resource_callback_invoked(cb, _, _, _, u); the x = 0 premise stays (the reuse arm still refuses). The OpenSSL checker derives and requires the new clause set; contracts.lock re-pinned (the two pem digests only). Lean QCore.CallbackLiteralPremise (21 audited theorems). Measured: the opt-in current run over the OpenSSL callers' seven files moves no row and changes 4 rows' content: rdkafka_ssl.c:761, 833 now refuse callback-uncontracted (rd_kafka_transport_ssl_passwd_cb), rdkafka_cert.c:349, 405 the member store of the result; the null-cb reads (Monkey tls_load_builtin_credentials, the predecessor fixture's read_cert, Pending to Unknown) now refuse callback-undecided, as predicted (OPENSSL-PEM-NULL-CALLBACK-DEFAULT). Pinned routes cannot move by construction (no premise beside an invocation exists in a pinned set, and none reads the user load path); the declared arbiter is the integrator's.

ledger.why: DISCHARGED by OPENSSL-PEM-CALLBACK-ARM (2026-11-18): the loader admits a literal-argument premise beside synchronous invocations only (C04.5, C04.19, G05, rule 57), route G's premise rewrite reaches withheld retaining declarations (measured necessary: without it the reuse arm was Safe), QCore.CallbackLiteralPremise audited, pem.qv states resource_callback_invoked(cb, _, _, _, u) beside the x premise, checker shape and lock follow. Of the seven librdkafka calls only rdkafka_ssl.c:790 (&ca at x, the reuse arm) stays outside the premise; the remaining blockers are callback-uncontracted (rdkafka_ssl.c:761, 833), member stores of the result (rdkafka_cert.c:349, 405) and calls in loop or branch conditions (rdkafka_cert.c:272, rdkafka_ssl.c:790, 1292). The null-cb arm regressed in content (OPENSSL-PEM-NULL-CALLBACK-DEFAULT).

ledger.title: PEM readers called with a null password callback
ledger.text: Registered by OPENSSL-PEM-CALLBACK-ARM. With cb stated as resource_callback_invoked(cb, _, _, _, u), a null pointer constant at cb is an open candidate set (rule 13u, callback-undecided), while OpenSSL documents the null-cb arm as the default callback routine (or u read as the passphrase), invoking no caller function. The calls the retired cb = 0 premise covered therefore refuse: Monkey tls_load_builtin_credentials (tls_openssl.c:176, 188; its six X509_free/EVP_PKEY_free drops return to reference-drop-unheld), the OIDC assertion (rdkafka_sasl_oauthbearer_oidc.c:495, 498), and OPENSSL-PROVIDER-REMAINING-CALLEES' fixture read_cert (Pending to Unknown). One declaration per function cannot keep both arms. DISCHARGE (user decision): a clause or invocation qualifier stating that a null F invokes nothing (the callee's own default), in the loader, rule 13u's candidate resolution (null as the empty set only under that qualifier), Lean QCore.CallbackContracts parity, and pem.qv; or accept the refusal.

ledger.title: librdkafka's PEM password callbacks as contracted candidates
ledger.text: Registered by OPENSSL-PEM-CALLBACK-ARM (opt-in current run at 046accf6). rd_kafka_ssl_PKEY_from_string and rd_kafka_ssl_X509_from_string (rdkafka_ssl.c:761, 833) refuse callback-uncontracted: rd_kafka_transport_ssl_passwd_cb has no validated summary (it calls rd_kafka_dbg and rd_kafka_log). rd_kafka_conf_ssl_passwd_cb (rdkafka_cert.c:51) is reached at rdkafka_cert.c:349, 405 only behind the member store cert->x509 / cert->pkey of the returned reference (indirect memory access is outside the resource projection); rdkafka_cert.c:272 and rdkafka_ssl.c:1292 call the reader in a while condition and rdkafka_ssl.c:790 in an if condition (unmodeled call in a condition). DISCHARGE: an identity contract in force for rd_kafka_transport_ssl_passwd_cb (its logging contracted or a declared summary), and the member-store and condition-call readings, measured on the opt-in run.
